solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Announced permission to go through baptism, for example (4,2,7)

indicatorNotes.Announced: what is announced is spoken out, so you go by the sound, not the spelling

blocks.note: a right of passage lets you cross; RITE sounds the same as RIGHT

annotation.surface: Someone declares that you are cleared to pass, perhaps at a christening.
annotation.walkthrough: Only the first word changes: RIGHT and RITE are said the same, while OF PASSAGE is spelt identically in both phrases.
annotation.definitionFit: A rite of passage is a ceremony marking a stage of life, and baptism marks entry into the church.

entries.clue: Political questions from priest, very lost for fine answer (9)

indicatorNotes.lost for: V is lost and F takes its place, as one thing is given up for another

blocks.note: a reverend is a member of the clergy
v = very; this V is swapped out
f = fine, as on pencil grades; it replaces the V, giving REFEREND

annotation.surface: A priest has lost his way and is looking for a good answer to some political questions.
annotation.walkthrough: Referenda is the Latin plural of referendum, a vote put to the whole electorate on one question.
annotation.definitionFit: Each referendum puts a single political question to the voters.

entries.clue: Person who changes views when advantageous better turned out (7)

annotation.definition: Person who changes views when advantageous

blocks.clueFragment: Person who changes views when advantageous
blocks.note: an opportunist who adjusts his sails to whichever political wind is blowing
neater in appearance, the comparative of an adjective meaning tidy

annotation.surface: A political turncoat turns out to be the better dressed man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned out' looks like a verb of changing sides, echoing the turncoat; here it means dressed, as in well turned out. Trim means neat, so trimmer is neater.
annotation.definitionFit: A trimmer is an old name for an opportunist who adjusts his principles to suit the times.

entries.clue: Pretended to be missing, first off: showing good judgment, just the same (10)

indicatorNotes.first off: the first letter is taken off
indicatorNotes.just the same: the same treatment is given again, so the next word also loses its first letter

blocks.clueFragment: showing good judgment, just the same

annotation.surface: Someone faked being lost, which showed good sense after all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Just the same' reads as 'nevertheless'; it is an instruction to repeat 'first off' on the second word.
annotation.definitionFit: Ostensible means professed or apparent rather than real, as a pretended reason is.

entries.clue: Forgo second drink, following assistant (4,2)

indicatorNotes.following: second and drink come after the assistant

annotation.surface: Someone declines another drink after their assistant has had one.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay is read backwards: the assistant comes first in the answer although it is last in the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: turning down a chance you are offered is going without it.

entries.clue: Policy, ignoring home, includes covering large watch (12)

indicatorNotes.ignoring: IN is ignored, so it drops out
indicatorNotes.includes: what is left holds VEIL and L inside it

blocks.note: in = at home; removed from the front to leave SURANCE
l = large, as on clothing sizes

annotation.surface: An insurance policy that excludes the home still covers large items.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is pure insurance jargon: home, covering, large. 'Watch' is the sense of keeping a close eye on someone.
annotation.definitionFit: Surveillance is close observation of a suspect, keeping watch.

entries.clue: Player grabbing character from behind: it gets things moving (8)

indicatorNotes.grabbing: ACTOR grabs the letters and holds them inside
indicatorNotes.from behind: the character is read from its back end, so TAU becomes UAT

blocks.note: tau is a Greek letter, a character; reversed to UAT and put inside ACT…OR

annotation.surface: An actor grabs a stagehand from behind, and that gets the scene moving.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a role for the player; it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: An actuator is the part of a machine that turns a signal into movement.

entries.clue: Hence hesitant dismissal? (4)

blocks.note: er is the sound of hesitation

annotation.surface: A hesitant boss finally sends someone away.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that 'Go!' is a command of dismissal rather than a dismissal itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A Latin word for therefore, used in English logic to introduce a conclusion.

entries.clue: Very much in debt for computer deliveries (9)

blocks.note: to be down is to be out of pocket

annotation.surface: Someone has run up huge debts buying things for their computer.
annotation.walkthrough: The two parts sit in reverse order in the clue: 'Very much' becomes the end of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Downloads are files delivered to your computer over the internet.

entries.clue: Part of address of monk with a hot reputation (6,4)

blocks.note: Dom is the title of a Benedictine monk
to make a name for yourself is to win a reputation

annotation.surface: A monk famous for his fiery reputation makes a speech.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Address' reads as a speech or a postal address; it is a web address, whose domain name is the example.com part.
annotation.definitionFit: The domain name is the part of a web address that names the site.

entries.clue: Complain joint is under weight (6)

indicatorNotes.is under: in a down answer, what is under comes below, so the joint follows the W

blocks.note: a hinge is a joint on a door

annotation.surface: Someone moans that their aching joint is carrying too much weight.
annotation.walkthrough: To whinge is British slang for a persistent, peevish moan.
annotation.definitionFit: Whinge means to complain in a whining way.

entries.clue: Some wealth in vintage wine perhaps, but not in vintage cars? (6,6)

annotation.definition: Some wealth in vintage wine perhaps, but not in vintage cars?

blocks.clueFragment: Some wealth in vintage wine perhaps
blocks.note: the surface suggests a collector's cellar; the setter means wealth held in a form that is literally a liquid
old cars are solid and slow to sell, so neither literally nor financially liquid

annotation.surface: A collector weighs up whether to invest in fine wine or classic cars.
annotation.walkthrough: Liquid assets are holdings easily turned into cash; the clue plays on wine being a liquid in the everyday sense too.
annotation.definitionFit: Wine is a liquid you own, and liquid assets are the part of your wealth that can be sold quickly.

entries.clue: Creating fear, having little hope on this, with a prayer (5)

annotation.definition2: having little hope on this, with a prayer
annotation.definitionNote: the second definition gives the phrase A WING, completing 'on a wing and a prayer'

blocks.clueFragment: having little hope on this, with a prayer
blocks.note: completes a saying about slim hopes: on ___ and a prayer

annotation.surface: Someone frightening, pinning slim hopes on a prayer.
annotation.walkthrough: The saying 'on a wing and a prayer' comes from a wartime song about a damaged plane limping home; 'this' stands for the missing A WING.
annotation.definitionFit: To awe someone is to fill them with reverent fear, so awing is creating fear.

entries.clue: Moves to discredit American maps, poorly covering golf (5,8)

indicatorNotes.poorly: AMERICAN MAPS are rendered badly, so their letters are out of order
indicatorNotes.covering: the rearranged letters cover G, holding it within

blocks.note: Golf is G in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Badly drawn American maps are spread over a golf course.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all cartography and golf; nothing in it hints at politics until the definition is read as a noun phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: A smear campaign is a series of moves designed to discredit an opponent.

entries.clue: Pass off clenched hand having nothing in it (5)

indicatorNotes.having: a hand having something is holding it, so the fist contains what follows
indicatorNotes.in it: and the thing it has sits inside it

blocks.note: a fist is a clenched hand
O looks like a zero, nothing

annotation.surface: A conjuror shows a closed fist that turns out to be empty.
annotation.walkthrough: The picture is a magician's trick, which suits the definition: foisting is passing off something false.
annotation.definitionFit: To foist a fake on someone is to pass it off as genuine.

entries.clue: Wheeze, returning from exam eg at art school (9)

indicatorNotes.returning: the letters are read going back, right to left
indicatorNotes.from: the answer is taken out of the words that follow

blocks.note: exaM EG AT ART School, read right to left

annotation.surface: A student comes back from an art school exam with a breathless story.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wheeze' suggests a breathless student; in British slang a wheeze is a clever scheme or trick.
annotation.definitionFit: A wheeze is a crafty plan, and a stratagem is a scheme to outwit someone.

entries.clue: Seek information from contents of tiny pile of paper (7)

indicatorNotes.contents of: the contents of a word are its inside letters

blocks.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

annotation.surface: Someone digs through a small stack of papers looking for facts.
annotation.walkthrough: QUIRE is an old measure of paper, a twentieth of a ream.
annotation.definitionFit: To inquire is to ask questions, seeking information.

entries.clue: What could indicate hour of novelist our realm viciously suppresses (5,7)

indicatorNotes.viciously: OUR REALM is savaged, its letters thrown about
indicatorNotes.suppresses: the jumbled letters hold the novelist down inside them

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters, arranged around MANN

annotation.surface: A writer complains that the country is savagely censoring him.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the hour on a clock face, where XII or IV may mark the time.
annotation.definitionFit: Many clock faces use Roman numerals, so one could indicate the hour.

entries.clue: Circus more splendid after installing good place for band (4,6)

indicatorNotes.after: the splendid part comes after the circus
indicatorNotes.installing: FINER has G installed inside it

annotation.surface: A circus becomes grander after booking a good spot for the band to play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians under the big top; it is a wedding band, worn on the ring finger.
annotation.definitionFit: A wedding ring, or band, is traditionally worn on the ring finger.

entries.clue: Like some walking old way through six counties — cold (6)

indicatorNotes.through: the old way runs through the six counties, sitting inside them

blocks.note: Northern Ireland is made up of six counties

annotation.surface: A hiker follows an old path across Northern Ireland in chilly weather.
annotation.walkthrough: Nordic walking uses a pair of poles, like cross-country skiing without the snow.
annotation.definitionFit: Nordic walking is a fitness style using ski-like poles, so the answer describes some walking.

entries.clue: After short glance, noticed daughter not occupied at this (5,3)

indicatorNotes.short: the glance is cut short, losing its last letter
indicatorNotes.After: the rest follows the shortened glance

annotation.surface: A parent glances over and sees their daughter has nothing to do.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the idiom: someone with nothing to do is at a loose end, so 'this' stands for the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Being at a loose end means having nothing to occupy you.

entries.clue: Reworked and hence improved (8)

indicatorNotes.Reworked: the letters are worked over into a new order

annotation.surface: A draft was reworked and so got better.
annotation.walkthrough: 'And hence' reads as a logical link joining two verbs; it is the whole of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something enhanced has had its quality raised.

entries.clue: No case for illegal trade with a tropical product (6)

indicatorNotes.No case for: the word loses its case, its outer letters

blocks.note: traffic is illegal dealing, as in drug traffic; losing T and C leaves RAFFI

annotation.surface: A lawyer says there is no case against someone smuggling tropical goods.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No case' sounds like a court ruling; it strips the outer letters off TRAFFIC.
annotation.definitionFit: Raffia is fibre from the leaves of a tropical palm, used for weaving and tying.

entries.clue: Let a man go who acts without restraint (4,5)

annotation.definitionNote: a relative clause standing for the person who does this

blocks.note: to let go is to free; 'go' completes the phrase

annotation.surface: A prisoner is released and now does as he pleases.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Let go' wraps around 'a man', as in 'let a man go', so the verb splits in the clue but reads as one piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A free agent is someone who can act as they choose, answerable to nobody.

entries.clue: Voracious, finally seize certain books I must open (8)

indicatorNotes.open: I opens up the letters and goes inside them

blocks.note: NT = New Testament, books of the Bible
as printed; goes inside SURE NT as SUR(I)ENT

annotation.surface: A greedy reader grabs certain books and insists on opening them himself.
annotation.walkthrough: Esurient is a rare, literary word for greedy, from the Latin for being hungry.
annotation.definitionFit: Esurient means hungry or greedy, which is voracious.

entries.clue: Spaniard with a Welsh girl — as they say, ladies first (10)

indicatorNotes.as they say: go by the sound of what people say
indicatorNotes.first: the ladies come before the Welsh girl

blocks.note: the ladies is a women's toilet, a loo; written as it is said
Sian is a common Welsh girl's name

annotation.surface: A Spaniard escorts a Welsh girl, politely letting women go first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ladies first' reads as good manners; it also places the loo before SIAN. In Britain the ladies is the women's toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: An Andalusian comes from Andalusia in southern Spain.

entries.clue: Shamed, dig sacred ground (9)

indicatorNotes.ground: the letters are ground up, crushed into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone was shamed for digging up holy ground.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like the noun, land, completing 'sacred ground'; it is the verb, crushed.
annotation.definitionFit: Disgraced means brought into shame.

entries.clue: One has stacks to clean when my pieces crumble (7,5)

indicatorNotes.crumble: the pieces break apart and the letters fall into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone groans at the pile of cleaning they face when their things fall apart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stacks' suggests heaps of work; they are chimney stacks.
annotation.definitionFit: A chimney sweep's job is cleaning chimney stacks.

entries.clue: Harsh demand for money in divorce case? (8)

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse
a legal action is a case in court

annotation.surface: A spouse makes a punishing claim for money during divorce proceedings.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose reading: an ex's action is a divorce case, and 'in' only joins the parts.
annotation.definitionFit: An exaction is a harsh or unjust demand, especially for payment.

entries.clue: Stress vote for the left? (8)

blocks.note: to dwell on a point at excessive length
a two-word plea to side with Britain's main left-wing party

annotation.surface: A canvasser keeps pressing the case for voting left.
annotation.walkthrough: The Labour Party is Britain's main party of the left, so 'be Labour' is a call to vote for it.
annotation.definitionFit: Overemphasis: you labour a point by going on about it long after it is made.

entries.clue: Head off accident? Not careful enough (4)

indicatorNotes.Head off: the head, the first letter, comes off

annotation.surface: A driver tries to prevent a collision but is too careless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head off' reads as prevent; it means cut the first letter off.
annotation.definitionFit: A rash act is one done without enough care or thought.

entries.clue: Avoid female authors, with TLS heartlessly making small changes (13)

indicatorNotes.heartlessly: TLS loses its heart, the middle L

blocks.note: to avoid women writers, READ JUST MEN

annotation.surface: A literary reviewer at the TLS shuns women writers and coldly tweaks their copy.
annotation.walkthrough: The TLS is the Times Literary Supplement, a British book review paper. 'Avoid female authors' is a playful phrase for READ JUST MEN.
annotation.definitionFit: Readjustments are slight alterations made to set something right again.

entries.clue: Disclaim holding corps, disloyal no longer (8)

annotation.definitionNote: 'no longer' marks the answer as an archaic word for disloyal

indicatorNotes.holding: RECANT holds the corps inside it

blocks.note: to recant is to take back what you said
RE = Royal Engineers, an army corps

annotation.surface: A soldier renounces his old regiment and swears he is no longer a traitor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Disloyal no longer' reads as a reformed traitor; 'no longer' says the word is out of use.
annotation.definitionFit: Recreant is an old word for unfaithful or cowardly, a deserter of a cause.

entries.clue: Old sheep with one shoulder cut cured (8)

blocks.note: a ram is a male sheep
I is the Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: A butcher takes an old sheep and cures a cut of its shoulder.
annotation.walkthrough: The sheep invites lamb or mutton; pastrami is spiced, smoked beef.
annotation.definitionFit: Pastrami is a cut of beef, often shoulder or brisket, that has been cured and smoked.

entries.clue: Standing quietly, nothing grand here (7,5)

blocks.note: piano is the musical direction for playing softly

annotation.surface: Someone stands silently in a modest room with nothing impressive in it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nothing grand' reads as humble; it says this piano is not a grand piano.
annotation.definitionFit: An upright piano stands vertically, the alternative to a grand.

entries.clue: Irish revolutionary moving left holds news channels beyond salvation (12)

indicatorNotes.moving left: the L of REBEL moves one place to the left
indicatorNotes.holds: the altered rebel holds the channels inside it

blocks.note: a rebel is a revolutionary; with L moved left it is REBLE
the media carry the news; held as RE(MEDIA)BLE

annotation.surface: An Irish rebel shifts his politics leftwards and captures the newspapers, a hopeless cause.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Moving left' reads as a political shift; it moves the letter L one step to the left.
annotation.definitionFit: Irremediable means impossible to cure or put right.

entries.clue: Songs went high up at this rate (8)

blocks.note: 'went' as a euphemism for going to the toilet

annotation.surface: Some tunes soared high at a great pace.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Went' is the coy sense of relieving yourself, as in 'I need to go'.
annotation.definitionFit: Airspeed is the rate at which an aircraft moves through the air, high up.

entries.clue: River creature in land legally acquired by temple (5,3)

indicatorNotes.acquired by: the temple acquires the land and takes it inside

blocks.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia
terra is the Latin word for land used in legal phrases

annotation.surface: A river animal lives on land a temple bought legally.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Legally' tells you to use the Latin of legal documents, where land is terra.
annotation.definitionFit: The water rat, or water vole, lives on riverbanks, like Ratty in The Wind in the Willows.

entries.clue: Nobody has energy to move something inert (4)

indicatorNotes.to move: the E is moved to a different spot

blocks.note: the E of NONE moves up to second place

annotation.surface: Nobody can be bothered to shift a lump that won't budge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Energy' reads as get-up-and-go; it is the E already in NONE, which is moved.
annotation.definitionFit: Neon is one of the inert or noble gases, which hardly react with anything.

entries.clue: Bull in mortuary? (4,6)

blocks.note: the bull is the bullseye, the exact middle of a target
a mortuary is a centre for the dead

annotation.surface: A bull has somehow ended up in a morgue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bull' looks like the animal; in darts and shooting it is the bullseye.
annotation.definitionFit: The bull is the exact middle of a target, its dead centre.

entries.clue: Immunity may be so complex to claim with depression on top (10)

indicatorNotes.complex: the letters are made complicated, rearranged
indicatorNotes.on top: in a down answer, the depression sits above the rest

annotation.surface: Claiming immunity is complicated if you are feeling low.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests mood; it is a dip in the ground.
annotation.definitionFit: Diplomatic immunity shields envoys from prosecution in the country where they serve.

entries.clue: Sailor apparently ready for burial who suddenly jumps up (4-2-3-3)

annotation.definitionNote: a relative clause standing for the thing that does this

blocks.note: Jack, or Jack Tar, is a sailor
someone in a coffin looks ready to be buried

annotation.surface: A sailor laid out in his coffin suddenly sits bolt upright.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a horror film joke: a corpse leaping up, which is exactly what the toy does.
annotation.definitionFit: A jack-in-the-box is a toy figure that springs up out of its box when the lid opens.

entries.clue: Noticed his failing, pleasure-seeking (10)

indicatorNotes.failing: the letters break down and fall into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone spotted a friend's weakness for the good life.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Failing' looks like a noun, a flaw; it is a verb telling you the letters collapse.
annotation.definitionFit: Hedonistic means devoted to the pursuit of pleasure.

entries.clue: Church never more pessimistic? (9)

blocks.note: the opposite of 'ever more' is 'ever less', with ever shortened to poetic E'ER

annotation.surface: A gloomy churchgoer declares nothing will ever get better.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Never more' is turned inside out to 'e'er less'; the question mark covers both that twist and the loose definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone cheerless is gloomy, much as a pessimist is.

entries.clue: Some underwear poet hasn’t finished wearing (8)

indicatorNotes.hasn’t finished: the poet's name stops short of its last letter

blocks.note: a bra is an item of underwear

annotation.surface: A poet is caught only half dressed, wearing a bit of underwear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' reads as dressed in; it is the sense of wearing away, as sandpaper does.
annotation.definitionFit: An abradant wears surfaces down by rubbing, like an abrasive.

entries.clue: Miserable day and hour regularly for holy man (6)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at regular intervals, every other one

annotation.surface: A miserable day and hour pass for a holy man at prayer.
annotation.walkthrough: A saddhu, or sadhu, is a Hindu holy man who has given up worldly life.
annotation.definitionFit: Saddhu is a variant spelling of sadhu, a wandering Hindu ascetic.

entries.clue: Gorgeous bachelor leaves crowd in aftermath of a party (8)

indicatorNotes.leaves: the B leaves the word, dropping out
indicatorNotes.in aftermath of: the crowd comes after the party

annotation.surface: A handsome single man slips out of the crowd after a party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gorgeous bachelor' reads as one phrase; the bachelor is only the B that goes.
annotation.definitionFit: Adorable means delightful and lovable, and gorgeous can mean just that.

entries.clue: Very happy building’s first illuminated by helium (6)

indicatorNotes.first: only the first letter of building

blocks.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium

annotation.surface: A building lit up by helium lamps looks cheerful.
annotation.walkthrough: The science picture of helium lighting hides three quick abbreviations.
annotation.definitionFit: Blithe means carefree and joyful.

entries.clue: On application, obtain date (4,3)

blocks.note: a patent, licence or loan is obtained by applying for it
to take someone out is to go on a date with them

annotation.surface: Someone fills in a form to get a date.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Date' looks like a calendar day; it is the verb, to court someone.
annotation.definitionFit: To take out a loan or policy is to obtain it after applying.

entries.clue: One fleeced, put up initially across better city (6)

indicatorNotes.put up: in a down answer, putting up reads the letters from bottom to top
indicatorNotes.initially: only the first letter of across

blocks.note: to cap a story is to better it
LA = Los Angeles; CAP LA reversed gives ALPAC

annotation.surface: A swindled gambler raises a stake on a city bet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fleeced' suggests cheated, but the alpaca is literally shorn of its fleece.
annotation.definitionFit: Alpacas are South American animals kept and sheared for their wool.

entries.clue: Long to throttle editor, a nit-picker (6)

indicatorNotes.to throttle: PANT grips the editor round the neck, holding it inside

blocks.note: to pant for something is to long for it

annotation.surface: A writer wants to strangle the editor who fusses over every detail.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface paints the author's revenge on a fussy editor, and the editor is also the nit-picker it describes.
annotation.definitionFit: A pedant fusses over small details, as a nit-picker does.

entries.clue: After second refusal, I cut into staff’s legal rights (10)

indicatorNotes.After: the rest follows the second and refusal
indicatorNotes.cut into: I cuts its way inside the staff's

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a pole is a staff, and staff's gives POLE'S

annotation.surface: After a second refusal, someone cuts into the workforce's rights.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees; it is a pole, a long stick.
annotation.definitionFit: A monopoly can be an exclusive legal right to trade in something, as a patent grants.

entries.clue: Part of minor thoroughfare that is magnetically attractive (5)

annotation.definitionNote: a relative clause standing for the direction

indicatorNotes.Part of: the answer is only part of the words that follow

annotation.surface: A little side street has some magnetic charm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Magnetically attractive' reads as charm; it means a compass needle is drawn towards magnetic north.
annotation.definitionFit: A compass needle is pulled towards the magnetic north.

entries.clue: Mean bracket I carved as woodworker (7-5)

indicatorNotes.carved: the letters are cut up and reshaped

annotation.surface: A carpenter admits he carved a rather poor shelf bracket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carved' suits the woodworking picture exactly while quietly telling you to rearrange the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A cabinet-maker is a skilled woodworker who makes fine furniture.

entries.clue: Greens joined by a star (4)

annotation.surface: A plate of greens shares the bill with a celebrity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A star' reads as one phrase; the A goes into the answer and the star alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Vega is one of the brightest stars in the northern sky, in the constellation Lyra.

entries.clue: Bliss, having vehicle in wild rain (7)

indicatorNotes.having: the rain has the vehicle inside it
indicatorNotes.wild: the letters of RAIN run wild into a new order

blocks.note: a van is a vehicle; it sits inside the jumbled rain

annotation.surface: Being snug in your camper van during a storm is pure bliss.
annotation.walkthrough: The picture is a cosy van in a downpour; nirvana comes from the Buddhist state of perfect peace.
annotation.definitionFit: Nirvana is a state of perfect happiness, bliss.

entries.clue: A certain ploy gaining area for time in the country (3,6)

indicatorNotes.gaining: to gain something is to take it on, so the ploy takes A into itself
indicatorNotes.for: A comes in for, in place of, T

blocks.note: the definite article marks a certain one
a gambit is an opening ploy
t = time; swapped out, so GAMBIT becomes GAMBIA

annotation.surface: Someone tries a particular trick to buy land out of town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In the country' reads as rural; 'country' is the definition. The Gambia is a small West African nation.
annotation.definitionFit: The Gambia is a country in West Africa, whose name officially keeps the article.

entries.clue: Recurring idea for rejecting English wine (5)

indicatorNotes.rejecting: what is rejected is sent back, so the letters are read backwards

annotation.surface: A critic keeps turning down English wine as a matter of principle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rejecting' reads as snobbery about English wine; it sends E PORT back to front.
annotation.definitionFit: A trope is a recurring theme or motif in stories and art.

entries.clue: Up to 18, not keen about Henry wearing green (6-3)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so COOL wraps round the H
indicatorNotes.wearing: the result is worn inside the green

blocks.note: H is the henry, the unit of inductance; COOL around it is CHOOL
sage is a grey-green colour; it is worn outside CHOOL

annotation.surface: A teenager is lukewarm about a boy called Henry dressed in green.
annotation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a person's name; it is H, the physics unit.
annotation.definitionFit: Children under 18 are of school age, when they are expected to be in education.

entries.clue: Certifies I ate a chestnut that is bad (13)

indicatorNotes.bad: the letters have gone bad and come out in a new order

annotation.surface: Someone confirms that they ate a chestnut that had gone off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chestnut' suggests a stale joke as well as a nut; either way it is just fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: To authenticate a document or object is to certify that it is genuine.
